monthly.recommendation: Keep this layer disabled until large snapshots bypass avoidable serialization/copying or use a smaller faithful representation.

progress.recommendation: Review completed-entry capacity and use a repeatable larger workload before choosing limits.

responses.observation: One fast reused response is promising but not enough for latency acceptance.

limitations: No route/status/abort group has 100 samples; p95 values in reports are descriptive and cannot be used for acceptance.
Phases have unequal traffic (62 to 110 requests), different status mixtures and unknown profile coverage.
Phase starts were not included in aggregate exports; end times are source file modification times.
Host CPU steal was sampled after the phases and is not a historical measurement of their execution.
Staging runs background jobs in the API; production uses a separate worker.
The observed large monthly snapshot explains avoidable overhead in that stage, not the entire earlier production slowdown.
Functional checks were reported by the user; only normalized numeric telemetry was collected independently.

changes: Conservative bounded admission before V8 encoding, with 50000 visits, 64 levels and the existing 2 MiB entry bound.
Rejected results are returned only to their loader owner; pending followers calculate their own graph under their own revision/access context.
Up to eight LRU rejection markers hold only key/deadline metadata for at most 15 seconds; no DTO or failure is retained.
Actual encoded byte limits are still checked if admission allows a value. No period, calculation, public field or original source value was removed.
New admissionRejected/admissionMs metrics remain numeric and use fixed labels.

regressionBeforeFix.failure: The prior engine encoded/copied a value even when the admission callback rejected it.

limits: Synthetic benchmark measures large-result admission/copy overhead only, not production HTTP acceptance.
Declined snapshots do not reuse completed calculations across requests; concurrency must be compared with cache-off in staging.
The conservative check may decline a value whose actual V8 encoding would fit the byte bound.
Remaining cards latency, CPU steal, and progress-cache sizing are not resolved by this change.
Staging large-snapshot contract uses synthetic large import metadata and a long date window, not copied application data.
The final synthetic benchmark ran while other local checks were active; it is not a controlled throughput or production latency trial.
